A0044.title: Legal Action
A0044.definition: Taking legal measures to combat attackers.
A0044.description: Legal action is both an effective means of stopping ongoing harm and a deterrent through publicizing the results of enforcement. Currently, criminal statutes related to cybercrime include: Article 285 'Unauthorized Access to Computer Information Systems,' Article 286 'Destruction of Computer Information Systems,' Article 287 'Assisting in Information Network Crimes,' Article 253 'Infringement of Citizens' Personal Information,' Article 219 'Infringement of Trade Secrets,' etc. Additionally, Article 255 'Illegal Business Operations' and Article 217 'Copyright Infringement,' while not cybercrime-specific statutes, are frequently used in cybercrime convictions.
A0044.limitation: Legal action depends on a clear statutory basis, preservable evidence and measurable harm, plus the ability to identify the offender and establish jurisdiction. Attribution is difficult when attackers operate abroad, use anonymous infrastructure, or leave an incomplete evidence chain. Conduct such as web scraping must be tied to specific facts such as unauthorized access, system damage, personal-data acquisition, or illegal business activity, and enforcement can take considerable time.
